top_story: U.S. strikes across Iran on 24 July triggered Iranian attacks on American bases in Bahrain, Jordan, and Kuwait, widening the conflict beyond the Gulf even as Washington’s campaign was framed around punishing Tehran and the Houthis for Red Sea attacks. By 27 July, the White House had paused bombing after military leaders judged the operation had reached its practical limit and was straining munitions stocks, yet Tehran used the pause to project resilience by asserting control over the Strait of Hormuz and rejecting talks. In the occupied West Bank, Israel’s plan for an extensive military operation after a deadly settler attack was followed by settler assaults on Palestinian villages on 26 July, including the burning of two mosques, deepening fears of collective punishment and further erosion of civilian security. The regional picture is one of simultaneous escalation and constraint: military actions are spreading across borders, but the immediate effect is to harden political positions and intensify civilian vulnerability rather than create leverage for de-escalation.
